title: Lungs and breathing
examples: How do my lungs actually work when I breathe?
What is the job of the diaphragm in breathing?
Where does the oxygen go after I breathe it in?

explain.say: Today we will learn about how we breathe air into our bodies. We will look at the parts that help us breathe. You will learn about the diaphragm muscle today.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the lungs. Look at the trachea, the bronchus and the bronchioles. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
The diaphragm is a big muscle under your lungs. When it moves down, it helps you breathe in air. This movement makes space for your lungs to fill up. You can feel it move when you breathe.

draw.text: Diaphragm moves down to breathe in

explain.say: Inside your lungs, there are tiny air sacs called alveoli. These sacs are where the important gas exchange happens. They are like little balloons for air.

draw.text: Alveoli: Tiny air sacs in lungs

explain.say: When we breathe in, we take in oxygen from the air. The alveoli take this oxygen and send it to our blood. This oxygen helps all parts of your body work. It is very important gas.
When we breathe out, we let out carbon dioxide. This gas is waste that our body does not need. The alveoli release this waste gas into the air. This keeps our blood clean.
Think about blowing up a balloon. You use your lungs and diaphragm to push air out. You are using the same muscles to breathe out. You are pushing the air out slowly.

faq.q: Why do I breathe in and out? What is the purpose?
faq.a: We breathe to get oxygen into our blood and to get rid of waste gas. You might also ask: What is the job of breathing? Or: Why do I need to breathe?
asks: What is the purpose of breathing?
What does breathing do for my body?

faq.q: What exactly is the diaphragm and where is it located?
faq.a: The diaphragm is a large, dome-shaped muscle found right underneath your lungs. It helps create the pressure changes needed for breathing. You might ask: Where is the diaphragm muscle? Or: What does the diaphragm do?
asks: How does the diaphragm help me breathe?

faq.q: What are alveoli, and why are they so important?
faq.a: Alveoli are tiny, balloon-like air sacs inside your lungs. They are the special places where oxygen moves from the air into your blood. You could also ask: What happens in the alveoli? Or: Are alveoli important?
asks: What are the little air sacs in my lungs?
Where does the oxygen go in my lungs?

faq.q: What is the difference between oxygen and carbon dioxide?
faq.a: Oxygen is the gas we need to live and it goes into our blood. Carbon dioxide is a waste gas that our body must breathe out. You might ask: Which gas do I breathe out? Or: What is waste gas?
asks: What gas do I breathe out?

faq.q: Does the diaphragm work alone to make me breathe?
faq.a: No, the diaphragm works with the muscles between your ribs to help you breathe. Together, they change the volume of your chest. You could also ask: Do I need other muscles? Or: Is the diaphragm the only muscle?

facts: The diaphragm is a large muscle located beneath the lungs.
Oxygen moves from the air sacs into the blood.
Carbon dioxide is a waste gas that we breathe out.
Breathing in increases the space inside the chest.

quiz.say: Which muscle moves down to help you breathe in?
quiz.why: The diaphragm is the main muscle that moves down to increase chest space.

wrong.1: These muscles help, but the diaphragm is the primary muscle mentioned for the main action.
wrong.2: The lungs are the organs, not the muscle that moves.
wrong.3: Alveoli are the air sacs, not the muscle.

quiz.say: What gas do we take in from the air?
quiz.why: Oxygen is the gas that our blood needs to carry to our body parts.

wrong.0: While present, nitrogen is not the gas our body primarily uses for breathing.
wrong.1: Air is a mix of gases; oxygen is the specific gas we need.
wrong.3: Carbon dioxide is the waste gas we breathe out, not the gas we need.

quiz.say: When we breathe out, what gas do we release?
quiz.why: We release carbon dioxide because it is a waste product from our body's processes.

wrong.0: Releasing oxygen would mean we are wasting the gas we need to live.
wrong.1: Water vapour is also released, but carbon dioxide is the main waste gas we focus on.
wrong.2: Nitrogen is mostly left in the air and is not the main waste gas from respiration.
